senses.en: the quality of being bland and gracious or ingratiating in manner

examples.text: The diplomat handled the tense negotiation with a suavity that disarmed even his harshest critics.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suāvitās(달콤함)에서 왔습니다. 부드럽고 상냥한 태도입니다.

senses.en: inferior in rank or status

examples.text: Historians increasingly study the subaltern voices excluded from official colonial records.

senses.en: A subordinate.

examples.text: As a subaltern of 24, Neave was captured in the defence of Calais in May 1940.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 subalternus에서 왔습니다. 다른 사람 '아래의' 하급자라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: taking place within the mind and modified by individual bias

examples.text: a subjective judgment

origin.ko: 라틴어 subiectīvus에서 왔고 subject에 -ive가 붙었습니다. 개인의 마음 아래에 놓인 주관적인 것을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: make subservient; force to submit or subdue

examples.text: The empire sought to subjugate neighboring tribes and force them to pay tribute.

senses.en: put down by force or intimidation

examples.text: The occupying army moved quickly to subjugate the rebellious provinces.

origin.ko: 라틴어 subiugāre(멍에 아래 두다)에서 왔습니다. 소에게 멍에를 씌우듯 복종시킵니다.

senses.en: direct energy or urges into useful activities

examples.text: The poet sublimated her grief into a series of luminous elegies.

senses.en: make more subtle or refined

examples.text: Years of study helped sublimate his crude ambitions into a genuine scholarly vocation.

senses.en: change or cause to change directly from a solid into a vapor without first melting

examples.text: some salts sublime when heated

origin.ko: 라틴어 sublīmāre(들어 올리다)에서 왔습니다. 충동을 높은 활동으로 끌어올린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: inspiring awe

examples.text: sublime scenery

senses.en: of high moral or intellectual value; elevated in nature or style

examples.text: a sublime deed

senses.en: greatest or maximal in degree; extreme

examples.text: The sublime arrogance of the plan stunned even the project's staunchest supporters.

origin.ko: 라틴어 sublīmis(높이 들린)에서 왔습니다. 높이 솟아 경외감을 주는 숭고함입니다.

senses.en: lower in rank or importance

examples.text: The several kinds […] and subordinate species of each are easily known.

senses.en: rank or order as less important or consider of less value

examples.text: Art is sometimes subordinated to Science in these schools

senses.en: an assistant subject to the authority or control of another

examples.text: A good manager listens carefully to every subordinate, however junior.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 subōrdināre(아래 서열에 두다)에서 왔습니다. 서열이 아래인 하위의 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a writ issued by court authority to compel the attendance of a witness at a judicial proceeding; disobedience may be punishable as a contempt of court

examples.text: The committee issued a subpoena demanding that the executive appear and produce the company's records.

senses.en: serve or summon with a subpoena

examples.text: The witness and her records were subpoenaed

origin.ko: 라틴어 sub poena(벌을 받는 조건으로)에서 왔습니다. 소환장 첫머리의 문구에서 이름이 되었습니다.

senses.en: abjectly submissive; characteristic of a slave or servant

examples.text: The subservient aides never dared to contradict the dictator, whatever his mistakes.

senses.en: serving or acting as a means or aid

examples.text: Local institutions played a subservient role, existing mainly to carry out the ministry's directives.

origin.ko: 라틴어 subservire(아래에서 섬기다)에서 왔습니다. 굽실거리며 섬기는 모습입니다.

senses.en: wear off or die down

examples.text: The pain subsided

senses.en: sink to a lower level or form a depression

examples.text: the valleys subside

origin.ko: 라틴어 subsīdere(아래로 앉다)에서 왔습니다. 가라앉아 잦아든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: of considerable importance, size, or worth

examples.text: He inherited a substantial amount of money from his uncle.

senses.en: having substance or capable of being treated as fact; not imaginary

examples.text: the substantial world

senses.en: of good quality and condition; solidly built

examples.text: a substantial fence or wall

origin.ko: 라틴어 substantia(아래에 서 있는 것, 본질)에서 왔습니다. 실체가 탄탄해 상당하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: establish or strengthen as with new evidence or facts

examples.text: The investigators could not substantiate the allegations with any documentary evidence.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 substantiare(실체를 주다)에서 왔습니다. 증거로 실체를 부여해 입증한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: consider (an instance of something) as part of a general rule or principle

examples.text: The theory subsumes several earlier hypotheses under a single, more general principle.

senses.en: contain or include

examples.text: This new system subsumes the old one

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 subsūmere(아래에 취하다)에서 왔습니다. 더 큰 범주 아래로 포함시킨다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: An indirect or deceptive device or stratagem; a blind. Refers especially to war and diplomatics.

examples.text: How’s the spy hunt going? Uncovered any subterfuge?

origin.ko: 라틴어 subterfugere(몰래 달아나다)에서 왔습니다. 책임을 슬쩍 피하는 핑계와 속임수입니다.

senses.en: difficult to detect or grasp by the mind or analyze

examples.text: The difference between the tones is subtle, but you can hear it if you listen carefully.

senses.en: able to make fine distinctions

examples.text: a subtle mind

senses.en: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

examples.text: a subtle poison

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 subtil에서 왔고 라틴어 subtīlis(가늘게 짠)와 이어집니다. 올이 가늘어 포착하기 어렵다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Intending to subvert, overturn, undermine or debase.

examples.text: subversive influence

senses.en: A radical supporter of political or social revolution.

examples.text: The regime jailed anyone it labeled a subversive, including several respected novelists.

origin.ko: subvert에 -ive가 붙은 말입니다. 아래에서부터 뒤집어엎으려는 성질을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: cause the downfall of; of rulers

examples.text: subvert the ruling class

senses.en: destroy property or hinder normal operations

examples.text: The oppressive regime stays in power only as long as they manage to subvert the will of the people.

senses.en: corrupt morally or by intemperance or sensuality

examples.text: Critics charged that the lavish gifts were meant to subvert the integrity of the judges.

origin.ko: 라틴어 subvertere(아래에서 뒤집다)에서 왔습니다. 밑에서부터 뒤집어 무너뜨린다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: Following, next in order.

examples.text: Each succeeding generation inherited a slightly more fragile river ecosystem.

senses.en: briefly giving the gist of something

examples.text: You should give clear, succinct information to the clients.

origin.ko: 라틴어 succīnctus(허리띠로 걷어 올린)에서 왔습니다. 옷자락을 띠로 졸라맨 듯 간결하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: assistance in time of difficulty

examples.text: Aid workers brought food and succor to villagers cut off by the flood.

senses.en: help in a difficult situation

examples.text: The monastery had long succored travelers caught in the mountain storms.

senses.en: The right or chance to vote, express an opinion, or participate in a decision, especially in a democratic election.

examples.text: The movement campaigned for universal suffrage regardless of property or sex.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suffrāgium(지지, 투표권)에서 왔습니다. 의견을 지지하는 한 표를 뜻합니다.

senses.en: showing a brooding ill humor

examples.text: And sullen I forsook the imperfect feast.

senses.en: Gloomy; dismal; foreboding.

examples.text: a sullen atmosphere

origin.ko: 앵글로노르만어 soleyn(혼자인)에서 왔고 라틴어 sōlus(혼자)와 이어집니다. 혼자 틀어박혀 시무룩하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: make dirty or spotty, as by exposure to air; also used metaphorically

examples.text: She tried to sully her rival’s reputation with a suggestive comment.

origin.ko: 고대 영어 sylian(더럽히다)에서 왔습니다. 진흙이나 때를 묻혀 더럽힌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by oppressive heat and humidity

examples.text: The battlefield—an undulating, parched, and dusty expanse—is lying under the sultry sun of a July afternoon.

senses.en: sexually exciting or gratifying

examples.text: a sultry look

origin.ko: swelter(찌는 듯이 덥다)의 옛 변형 sulter에 -y가 붙은 말입니다. 푹푹 찌는 무더위입니다.

senses.en: the highest level or degree attainable; the highest stage of development

examples.text: Learning from others as from himself, he reached the summit of his development with his latest work.

senses.en: a meeting of heads of governments

examples.text: They met for an international summit on environmental issues.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 sommet(꼭대기)에서 왔고 라틴어 summum(맨 위)과 이어집니다. 가장 높은 지점입니다.

senses.en: old; no longer valid or fashionable

examples.text: The superannuated regulations had not been revised since the telegraph era.

senses.en: too old to be useful

examples.text: The factory kept a few superannuated machines running long after they should have been scrapped.

origin.ko: 라틴어 superannuatus(한 해 넘은)에서 왔습니다. 나이가 차서 낡고 구식이 되었다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy

examples.text: Now he was a sturdy, straw haired man of thirty with a rather hard mouth and a supercilious manner.

origin.ko: 라틴어 superciliōsus(거만한)에서 왔고 supercilium(눈썹)과 이어집니다. 눈썹을 치켜올리고 남을 내려다보는 모습입니다.

senses.en: concerned with or comprehending only what is apparent or obvious; not deep or penetrating emotionally or intellectually

examples.text: superficial similarities

senses.en: of, affecting, or being on or near the surface

examples.text: superficial burns

senses.en: of little substance or significance

examples.text: a few superficial editorial changes

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 superficiālis(표면의)에서 왔습니다. 겉 표면만 건드려 얕다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: more than is needed, desired, or required

examples.text: With a full rain suit, carrying an umbrella may be superfluous.

senses.en: serving no useful purpose; having no excuse for being

examples.text: The editor cut every superfluous adjective from the manuscript, and the prose improved at once.

origin.ko: 라틴어 superfluus(넘쳐흐르는)에서 왔습니다. 그릇을 넘어 흐를 만큼 지나쳐 불필요하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: take the place or move into the position of

examples.text: Those older products have been superseded by our new range.

origin.ko: 라틴어 supersedēre(위에 앉다)에서 왔습니다. 남의 자리 위에 앉아 대신한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: take the place or move into the position of

examples.text: Will online dictionaries ever supplant paper dictionaries?

origin.ko: 라틴어 supplantāre(발바닥 아래를 걸어 넘어뜨리다)에서 왔습니다. 발을 걸어 밀어내고 그 자리를 차지합니다.

senses.en: (used of persons' bodies) capable of moving or bending freely

examples.text: supple joints

senses.en: (used of e.g. personality traits) readily adaptable

examples.text: a supple mind

senses.en: Compliant; yielding to the will of others.

examples.text: a supple horse

origin.ko: 라틴어 supplex(무릎 꿇은, 순종하는)에서 온 프랑스어 souple에서 왔습니다. 몸을 굽히듯 유연하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: humbly entreating

examples.text: a suppliant sinner seeking forgiveness

senses.en: one praying humbly for something

examples.text: I touch your beard as a suppliant, embrace your knees, imploring you to have pity on my wretchedness.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 suppliant(간청하는)에서 왔고 supplicant와 같은 계열입니다. 무릎을 꿇고 비는 모습입니다.

senses.en: ask humbly (for something)

examples.text: He supplicated the King for clemency

origin.ko: 라틴어 supplicāre(무릎을 굽혀 빌다)에서 왔습니다. 몸을 낮춰 간청한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a hypothesis that is taken for granted

examples.text: The whole argument rests on the supposition that human behavior is basically rational.

senses.en: a message expressing an opinion based on incomplete evidence

examples.text: The supposition that Geoffrey had been chloroformed was a reasonable hypothesis at that stage of the disclosure.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suppositiō에서 왔습니다. 논의의 밑에 놓아둔 전제, 곧 가정입니다.

senses.en: An excessive amount of something.

examples.text: A surfeit of wheat is driving down the price.

senses.en: To supply (someone) with something to excess; to disgust (someone) through overabundance.

examples.text: Constant exposure to cheap sensational news can surfeit readers until they stop caring.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 surfaire(지나치게 하다)의 과거분사에서 왔습니다. 도를 넘어 과잉이 된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: inclined to anger or bad feelings with overtones of menace

examples.text: a surly waiter

origin.ko: sir(나리)에서 나온 sirly의 변형입니다. 나리처럼 거만하고 퉁명스럽다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: imagine to be the case or true or probable

examples.text: If, as I surmise, you see the ladies this evening, you might mention my intended visit.

senses.en: Thought, imagination, or conjecture, which may be based upon feeble or scanty evidence; suspicion; guess.

examples.text: This opinion, however, is merely a surmise, which may or may not be the case.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 surmettre(위에 얹다, 고발하다)의 과거분사에서 왔습니다. 증거 위에 얹은 짐작을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: get on top of; deal with successfully

examples.text: She had to surmount enormous obstacles to become the first in her family to attend college.

senses.en: be on top of

examples.text: A bronze statue of an eagle surmounted the stone gateway of the old courthouse.

origin.ko: 고대 프랑스어 surmonter(위로 오르다)에서 왔습니다. 장애물 위로 올라서서 이겨낸다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: marked by quiet and caution and secrecy; taking pains to avoid being observed

examples.text: He cast a surreptitious glance at the answers on his neighbor's desk.

origin.ko: 라틴어 surrēptīcius에서 왔고 surrepere(몰래 기어들다)와 이어집니다. 슬그머니 몰래 하는 일입니다.

senses.en: someone who takes the place of another person

examples.text: A mixture of horseradish and mustard often serves as a surrogate for wasabi.

senses.en: providing or receiving nurture or parental care though not related by blood or legal ties

examples.text: The old nurse became a surrogate mother to the orphaned children.

origin.ko: 라틴어 surrogāre(대신 뽑다)에서 왔습니다. 다른 사람 대신 선택된 대리인입니다.

senses.en: imagine to be the case or true or probable

examples.text: I suspect he is a fugitive

senses.en: regard as untrustworthy; regard with suspicion; have no faith or confidence in

examples.text: I suspect her true motives

senses.en: Viewed with suspicion; suspected.

examples.text: What I can do or offer is suspect.

origin.ko: 라틴어 suspicere(아래에서 올려다보다)에서 왔습니다. 의심스러운 눈으로 올려 본다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (of undissolved particles in a fluid) supported or kept from sinking or falling by buoyancy and without apparent attachment

examples.text: dust particles suspended in the air

senses.en: Hung from above.

examples.text: A single bulb, suspended from the rafters, lit the cellar with a weak yellow glow.
